attrs.evidence: A head receipt cannot hash itself. Inside the repository the commit binds it; in the ARTIFACT nothing did. GPT-5.6 copied the clean extraction, changed `decision.verdict` from promote to reject and nothing else, and check-mosaic, check-lineage and check-claim-ledger all exited 0 — so the assurance layer accepted two contradictory head receipts over one otherwise identical bundle, and the verdict was the least bound byte in the archive. The archive already shipped invariant-canonical.bundle, so the check needed no new material: scripts/verify-review-artifact.mjs verifies the bundle, clones it, resolves the canonical head, confirms the revision tag, and byte-compares every committed path against the extraction. THE RENDERED BRIEFS ARE COMPARED RATHER THAN EXEMPTED: the declared {{CLAIM_COUNT}} substitution is re-applied to the committed bytes, which proves the stronger statement — the shipped brief is exactly the rendering of the committed source under the count the committed ledger carries.
attrs.gap: INTERNAL CONSISTENCY, NOT AUTHENTICITY, and conflating them would be the whole value of the claim thrown away. An attacker who rewrites the receipt AND rebuilds the bundle passes this and always will: nothing is signed, nothing is timestamped, no root of trust exists. FAC-RECEIPT-AUTH is that record and stays open. Second: the check needs `git`, so it is the one gate in this lane that a node-only extraction cannot run — stated in the brief rather than discovered. Third: MUT-EXTRACTED-RECEIPT-ALTERED is observed by a different process from check-mosaic's §5b battery, because the attack is a filesystem operation and cannot be a deep-copy registry mutation.
attrs.prior_art: GPT-5.6's audit of INV-R8.1, §6. The distinction is the one SLSA draws between provenance completeness and provenance authenticity.
attrs.statement: A downloadable review artifact proves, from a bare extraction and the repository it ships, that every canonical file it contains — the head receipt included — is the exact bytes of the commit its bundle names, and that every other file is a declared build product.
